t: 3551 – Minimum Swaps to Sort by Digit Sum
o: Sort numbers by (digit sum, value) and count the minimum swaps, which equals n minus the number of cycles in the permutation mapping current positions to sorted positions. Distinct values make the target order unique. Example 3: [18,43,34,16] → target [16,34,43,18]; permutation cycles {0,3},{1,2} → swaps = 1+1 = 2.
k: Minimum swaps to realize a permutation = Σ(cycle_length − 1) = n − #cycles.
Comparator: digit sum, tie-break by value.

a.i: Compute each number's digit sum, derive the sorted order, build the position mapping, then walk cycles counting visited nodes.
s: Walk cycles of pos[i]; add cycleSize−1 per cycle.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; cycle walk is O(n).

w: Standard 'minimum swaps to sort' template applied to a custom comparator. Pitfall: the tie-break by value matters (example 3). Follow-up: count swaps if only adjacent swaps were allowed (that would be inversion count).
